exposure: in utero selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) exposure
outcome: diagnostic utility of capillary blood cartridge-based testing
diagnostic utility of point-of-care glucose testing
cohort: The study included neonates aged 37-41 weeks of gestation diagnosed with neonatal jitteriness within the first 72 hours of life and a control group of healthy neonates of the same gestational age without jitteriness.
finding: Point-of-care glucose testing using a bedside glucometer was found to be sufficient for the evaluation of neonatal jitteriness, as capillary blood cartridge-based testing did not offer additional diagnostic value.
mod_finding: Jittery neonates had a higher rate of emergency cesarean deliveries compared to healthy controls.
